tool_input.description: Read build stage summary for test rationale

findings.detail: The diff adds a new public function but tests/test_core.py is byte-identical to baseline: no success-path or ValueError test for percent_change exists, violating spec R12 and the target's CLAUDE.md rule of at least two tests per public function, and skipping the first step listed in plan.md. Expected: tests/test_core.py imports percent_change and adds at least the R1-R10 cases from plan.md; the build summary states the sandbox denied edits under tests/ even in the build stage, so the deny rule must be lifted for build or the orchestrator must add the tests, since a fix iteration will hit the same denial.
findings.title: percent_change ships with zero tests (R12 unmet)

findings.detail: The implementation returns (new - old) / old literally, so percent_change(-100, -50) evaluates to -0.5, while spec R6 asserts the result is 0.5; the spec's API section, plan.md and the recorded open-question assumption all mandate the literal formula with no abs(), so the code matches intent and the R6 example value is the error. Expected: a human corrects R6 to -0.5 (or deliberately switches to abs(old) as a semantic change) before any test pins the behaviour, otherwise the planned test_percent_change_negative_baseline will fail against correct code.
findings.title: Spec R6 contradicts its own formula for negative baseline
